controls.expert: 40/40 twice, bit-identical traces (0 diverged environments, 0 flips)

notes: Delaying either observation group by 4 control steps (67 ms at 60 Hz) drops the expert from 40/40 to 0/40 (-1.000, every case lost; the t interval degenerates to a point). Pen-state delay: 33 drops (median fall step 116) and 7 tail-spin failures; hand-state delay: 39 drops (median 83) and 1 tail-spin failure.

Compared with R-044's constant clamps (pen: median fall step 49), a pen-state delay keeps the pen about twice as long but still loses every case; delaying hand state is worse than clamping it (0/40 vs 1/40, 39 vs 22 drops), plausibly because delayed joint positions beside a live last_action give a self-inconsistent proprioceptive state.
Only one delay (4 steps) was run, so there is no dose-response: the latency at which the expert starts failing lies at or below 67 ms and is unmeasured.

Limitation kept from the protocol: a delayed group beside live groups is a temporal joint-distribution shift the expert never trained on; this characterizes this PPO checkpoint's sensitivity, not a feedback-bandwidth requirement for symbolic controllers.
Accounting: 160 episodes (4 processes x 40), 0 LLM calls; about 2 minutes of GPU time.
